label: STOPP J4
title: SGLT2 inhibitor with symptomatic low blood pressure
statement: Sodium glucose co-transporter (SGLT2) inhibitors (e.g., canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin) with symptomatic hypotension (risk of exacerbation of hypotension).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: SGLT2 inhibitors such as empagliflozin and dapagliflozin can lower blood pressure further in a person who already has low blood pressure with symptoms.

medicine_groups.name: SGLT2 inhibitors
medicine_groups.note: Combination products count and the combination is named. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.meets: A line that says the person has low blood pressure with symptoms such as dizziness on standing, or blood pressure readings that are low with symptoms recorded

options.words: Low blood pressure caused symptoms during this SGLT2 inhibitor course
There was no low blood pressure with symptoms during this course

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 years or older. If age is unknown and the other criteria apply, ask for age before confirming a finding. Suspect a finding when a Group A medicine (an SGLT2 inhibitor) is supplied and the record has a line showing symptomatic low blood pressure; cite the supply lines and that fact line. For a Group A supply, use the blood pressure and symptom assessment relevant to that supply. The pharmacist judges borderline readings alongside the symptoms. A borderline reading alone cannot confirm a finding. If low blood pressure is recorded and symptoms are unknown, report a possible finding and ask whether symptoms accompanied the low pressure. If there is no assessment of symptomatic hypotension, report a possible finding and ask whether low blood pressure caused symptoms during supply. Give no finding when the assessment excludes symptomatic hypotension, including a low reading explicitly recorded as asymptomatic.
cannot_be_seen: Whether the person feels dizzy or faints, the current blood pressure, fluid intake, and other medicines that lower blood pressure supplied elsewhere. Blood pressure lines may be missing from a pharmacy record.
ask_the_gp: A review of the blood pressure and of whether the SGLT2 inhibitor is still suitable.
